title: An equilibrium model of “global imbalances” and low interest rates
authors: RJ Caballero, E Farhi, PO Gourinchas
abstract: The sustained rise in US current account deficits, the stubborn decline in long-run real rates, and the rise in US assets in global portfolios appear as anomalies from the perspective of conventional models. This paper rationalizes these facts as an equilibrium outcome when different regions of the world differ in their capacity to generate financial assets from real investments. title: An Equilibrium Model of “Global Imbalances” and Low Interest Rates
abstract: This paper analyzes the persistent current account deficits in the United States, the declining long-run real interest rates, and the increasing significance of US assets in global portfolios through the lens of an equilibrium model. It posits that these phenomena arise due to differing financial asset generation capacities among global regions, and it extends the model to explain exchange rate and foreign direct investment trends.
